sources.title: Historical atlas: Austronesians, 4000 to 323 BCE
sources.note: Exact culture record austronesians; repeated broad Island Southeast Asian polygons. Earliest bounds 95.19 to 126.37 east, 9.18 south to 18.55 north; later versions omit the Philippines and alter eastern islands. Taiwan, Madagascar and the Pacific lie outside. Metadata is not migration chronology or a surveyed linguistic frontier. See identities.json.

sources.title: Bellwood, Fox and Tryon, The Austronesians in History: Common Origins and Diverse Transformations
sources.note: Direct ANU Press chapter, The Austronesians: Historical and Comparative Perspectives, 1995 volume, 2006 digital edition. Opening and concluding paragraphs: language family, later distribution, diverse transformations and rejection of uniform culture. Outdated population counts and racial terminology omitted. All volume chapters and mirrors are one underlying work for budget review.

sources.title: Sandra Oliveira and colleagues, Ancient genomes from the last three millennia support multiple human dispersals into Wallacea (2022)
sources.note: Direct full Nature Ecology & Evolution paper. Main opening: likely Taiwan dispersal 4000 to 4500 years ago, Wallacea inhabited tens of millennia earlier; abstract and Results: 16 ancient individuals, differing northern/southern histories and repeated admixture. Do not equate genes with language; sampled individuals extend well beyond atlas endpoint, stated publicly.

sources.title: Hsiao-chun Hung and colleagues, Preceramic riverside hunter-gatherers and the arrival of Neolithic farmers in northern Luzon (2022)
sources.note: Direct full Antiquity article. Cagayan Neolithic circa 4200 to 4000 BP; Nagsabaran 2016 trench 79 rice grains/fragments and 224 Job’s tears; Figure 2 Neolithic spindle whorls, adzes and jade bracelet; Figure 10 contrasting Metal Age objects. Existing preceramic people expressly distinguished from arriving farmers. All PDFs/repository mirrors same work.

sources.title: National Museum of Prehistory, Peinan Park permanent exhibition
sources.note: Direct official museum exhibition account. Dwellings face away from mountain toward Taitung plain; models and excavation drawings distinguish reconstructed appearance from surviving remains. Life in Peinan culture lists farming, hunting, fishing, carpentry, weaving, garments and food implements. Burial section: over 2000 slate coffins. Conservatively grouped with the 2025 Peinan jade exhibit account for regional museum work budget.

sources.title: National Museum of Prehistory, Taiwan jade maritime exchange exhibition, 16 January 2025
sources.note: Direct Chinese museum research summary: Peinan jade peak 3500 to 2500 years ago; over 5000 jades mostly from slate-coffin burials, little production waste; interpretation that specialist workshops near Fengtian supplied goods. Boat simulator explicitly a scholarly reconstruction using modern fabrication, not ancient surviving vessel. Grouped with Peinan permanent exhibit.

sources.title: Hsiao-chun Hung and colleagues, Ancient jades map 3000 years of prehistoric exchange in Southeast Asia (2007)
sources.note: Direct PNAS research paper, DOI 10.1073/pnas.0707304104. Discussion: Nagsabaran Fengtian-nephrite bracelet 1800 to 1500 BCE; Taiwan comparative bracelets; 500 BCE to 500 CE wider exchange; manufacturing debris at multiple sites, Khao Sam Kaeo recycled adze into pendant. Sourcing demonstrates movement of stone, not automatic ethnic/political identity.

sources.title: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, Lapita pottery category
sources.note: Direct museum category using Getty Art and Architecture Thesaurus: toothed stamps build elaborate geometric motifs, sometimes faces; pottery figures; style named for New Caledonian site. Does not supply all Lapita dates or claim a writing system.

sources.title: Rebecca Kinaston and colleagues, Lapita Diet in Remote Oceania (2014)
sources.note: Direct PLOS original and abstract read; 49 Teouma adults, dietary protein includes reef/inshore foods, domestic animals, fruit bats; cemetery circa 3000 to 2900 BP. Existing Vanuatu runtime uses ANU repository mirror a1b80374-c9c9-4274-bd0d-2fe17629ed30; canonical reuse checker explicitly combines these as the same work. No added nursing, medicine or toilet claims.

sources.title: Cosimo Posth and colleagues, Language continuity despite population replacement in Remote Oceania (2018)
sources.note: Direct scholarly paper; ancient DNA and linguistic evidence for substantial later Near Oceanian ancestry with Austronesian language continuity in Vanuatu. Avoids assuming a genetic sample reveals the language spoken by a particular skeleton; no racial classifications or fixed ancestry percentages in prose.

sources.title: National Museum of Prehistory, Summoning the Ocean: Amis bamboo raft interpretation
sources.note: Direct museum text at 召喚海洋. Reconstruction based on Japanese castaway account of 1803 eastern Taiwan Amis community, narrated to artist after return: split bamboo, woven bamboo sail, rear platform for food preparation, two or three fishers. Museum retelling, not first-hand inspection of original Japanese manuscript; explicitly much later than map.

sources.title: Indigenous Languages Research and Development Foundation, Nanshi Amis 2026 learning vocabulary
sources.note: Indexed institutional original checked twice; direct PDF fetch 500. Printed page 9 of 77, entry 110 / 05-05, 孩童 wawa. PDF heading 南勢阿美語 2026年公告版. Modern Roman-letter orthography of this Amis variety, not a prehistoric Proto-Austronesian inscription. Query site:ilrdf.org.tw 2026年公告版 05-05 wawa 南勢阿美語; table extraction repeats entry 110 alongside subsequent entries, but wawa/孩童 pairing is consistent.

sources.title: Indigenous Languages Research and Development Foundation, toʉsvʉsvʉtʉ, issue 4: Education and Transmission
sources.note: Official indexed English PDF, printed pages 22 to 23, Education and Transmission: teaching aids, WAWA Touch Games, LIMA audiobooks, open platforms, animations and classroom videos. Data explicitly through August 2024. Direct PDF fetch failed; no unsupported visitor statistics used.

proposedOverrides.name: Austronesian-speaking peoples and maritime networks
proposedOverrides.summary: A diverse language family linked by migration and exchange, not one state.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: No aliases. Keep Malays, Malagasy, Māori, Taiwan and all particular Southeast Asian/Polynesian states distinct. Lapita material tradition is a regional archaeological comparison, not equivalent to all Austronesian languages.
batchIdentityNotes.mapWarning: 4000 to 323 BCE culture record, early shapes broadly western Indonesia plus Philippines; Taiwan, Madagascar and Pacific excluded, later shapes omit Philippines. Not actual migration front or ethnicity map.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Modern dated 2026 Nanshi Amis wawa (child), foundation vocabulary entry 110. No securely attested written Proto-Austronesian archive claimed. Roman orthography is the actual published modern sample. 1803 raft and 2024 education likewise explicitly later.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceReuse: 2014 Kinaston Teouma diet paper already used by Vanuatu via ANU repository; canonical work grouping implemented. Peinan museum pages conservatively grouped. No reuse detected for the other selected sources in initial evidence scan.
